chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn Sahl from Adam ibn Ali from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no Hajj or Jihad obligatory upon the slave, and he does not travel except with the permission of his master.
ai.seo_question: What are the obligations of Hajj and Jihad for a slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that while slaves are exempt from the obligatory duties of Hajj and Jihad, their physical mobility remains under the authority of their master, reflecting the socio-legal structure of the time. This ruling highlights the distinction between personal religious obligation and the master's right to control the slave's movement for service or trade. It underscores the practical application of fiqh in managing the status of slaves within the Islamic community.
